brain.summary: Not yet proven. The closest plan is "Only: Lodging-tax and occupancy filing workbook for bed-and-breakf", and what it is missing first is enough buyers, buying often enough, for the deals the plan needs. The reconstruction is hypothetical, not the plan: the reconstruction is flagged implausible (RETURN: median kept [figure withheld] is 11524× the [figure withheld] behind it (bound ×20)), so none of its figures is shown or adopted. The plan's steps are for "Lodging-tax and occupancy filing workbook for bed-and-breakfast inns".

facts.value: Brain estimates about 500 B&Bs in the region would buy a filing workbook each quarter.
Sell Lodging-tax and occupancy filing workbook for bed-and-breakfast inns to each buyer.
Innkeepers paid $175 each for the filing workbook (14 payment records, 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-23).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN with MARKET_VOLUME decisive is right. The only buyer count is Brain's own RECOMMENDATION (~500 B&Bs), an estimate, so the pool is not established. Price ($175, 14 payment records from innkeepers) and conversion (14/120 = 11.7%) are evidenced on this offer; Brain produces the workbook ($3), 4 days to cash. Arithmetic: $3,500 / $175 = 20 deals (at $172 net, 21 deals for net; gross 20 meets the received-cash proof condition); at 11.7% that is ~171 fresh contacts. The 14 buyers file quarterly and the next filing falls after the 30-day window, so repeat purchases are rightly not counted. The resolution - count innkeeper listings with emails on the state tourism board listings, the card's own channel - is a published-directory count research can settle; the gap is stated as a gap, not a constraint.
findings: The resolution threshold '~185 unsold listed innkeepers' should be ~171 uncontacted listings: the 106 contacted non-buyers should not be counted at 11.7%. Equivalently the listing must hold >= ~291 innkeepers with emails (120 already contacted + 171).
Brain's link says 16 deals needed while $3,500/$175 = 20; the plan's 20 is the correct figure for the full target.
